_structural_status: CHOSEN. These are design decisions and are now bound. train_baseline.py runs against them.
_measured_status: target_loss is NOT chosen and NOT bound. It is a measured property of where the baseline actually lands, so it stays null until a GPU run produces it. Choosing it would be inventing the number the whole task is scored against.

_derivation.method: C = 6 * N * D, with N counting only parameters that participate in a matmul, against a deliberately conservative 2.0e14 effective bf16 FLOP/s for a model this small. Small models get poor MFU, so assuming peak would have understated the time.
_derivation.baseline_reference: L=12 d=768 D=1.70e9 gives N=123.6M and C=1.26e18, which is 105 minutes on one H100. That independently reproduces the 1.4 to 2 GPU-hour per-run figure from the blog and the substrate's own cost target, which is why the model is trusted enough to size against.
_derivation.chosen: L=6 d=384 seq=512 D=6.0e7 gives N=29.9M and 54 s of training, plus about 9 s for 15 validation points over a 2M-token split, plus roughly 30 s of warmup and compile. Total about 93 s, inside the 90 to 110 s band.
_derivation.note_on_where_the_compute_actually_goes: Of the 29.9M matmul parameters, 19.3M is the output projection over the 50304 vocabulary and only 10.6M is the transformer body. At this width the vocabulary head dominates the cost, which is why shrinking depth and width alone gives far less speedup than parameter count suggests. This is the single most counterintuitive fact about the scaled point and it is why the token budget had to carry most of the reduction.

_rejected.reason: Rejected outright. The vocabulary is fixed by the tokenizer that produced the frozen dataset, so changing it would change the underlying token stream, which the substrate rules forbid and which would silently invalidate the frozen-data premise.
Rejected. N rises to 44.6M and training to 80 s, which pushes the total past 110 s once validation and warmup are added.

Rejected. Cheapest on paper at 40 s, but twice the sequential depth at a quarter the width gives materially worse MFU at this size, so the wall-clock saving is smaller than the FLOP count implies, and the extra depth buys nothing the task needs.
Rejected. Only 6 s cheaper than the chosen shape while making the model shallow enough that optimizer differences, which are the entire object of study, have less room to express themselves.
Rejected. 72 s of training pushes the total to about 111 s, just outside the band. The token budget is the dominant time term, so it is the lever that was tuned last and most carefully.

Rejected. Doubles activation memory and attention cost for no benefit at this scale, and the substrate explicitly names a sequence-length reduction as changing training, so a shorter sequence is a deliberate declared choice rather than an inherited invariance.

_bind_target_loss_by: Run train_baseline.py at this shape across the target-setting seeds, record the validation curve at the verifier-owned token grid, and set target_loss where the baseline lands with margin far wider than print precision. That binds anchors.json and re-triggers Phase 0.5, because it changes seed/contract.yaml.
